review.reviewer: GPT-6.1-Sol xhigh; independent static evidence review; no leaderboard scores consulted

architecture.rationale: Strong (3/4): cleanly separates document normalization/chunking/indexing, hybrid retrieval, agent assembly, middleware, schemas, transport and TUI. Pydantic decisions and a single shared process_ticket entry point keep the vertical slice understandable. Not exceptional: global mutable tracing/caches couple components to one process; permissive dictionary postprocessing weakens typed boundaries. Current CLI/TUI paths are serialized, so concurrency concerns are future risks rather than observed failures.

prompt_and_tool_design.rationale: Adequate-to-strong (2.5/4): explicit schema, classification boundaries, corpus-only grounding, search-read-cite sequence, escalation style and multilingual search guidance; real weighted BM25+dense retrieval with optional reranking and a constrained read-only search/read/grep interface. Half-point reflects substantive strengths offset by contradictions: stolen-card incidents appear in both escalation and reply guidance; mixed-intent support handling is requested but matched injection phrases unconditionally short-circuit; tool documentation makes reads conditional while the system makes them mandatory. No explicit trust boundary labels retrieved document text.

evidence.quote: canonical flow is always search -> read top hit -> reply.

robustness.rationale: Adequate (2/4): resolved-path containment, SQL quoting, safe escalation on model failure or missing structured output, classifier timeout/fallback, ingestion retries and reranker-to-RRF fallback are implemented. Material static defects prevent strong: citation guard accepts attempted failed reads and retains citation-less replies after any read; rerank cache stores positional indices against sorted-ID keys and omits top_n/content, allowing wrong/truncated or excessive result lists on reuse; 8-call cap is only a prompt plus graph recursion bound, with no overall wall-clock/token/cost enforcement. Retrieval arms lack independent fallback, index builds are not atomic or validated on reuse, read/regex budgets are incompletely bounded, and classifier cache I/O can escape the safe-fallback block. These are source-derived risks/logical consequences, not runtime reproductions.

experimental_rigor.rationale: Weak-to-adequate (1.5/4): readable documented modules, centralized settings, stable CSV serialization, per-ticket traces and a real sample-label/citation-length diagnostic script. Half-point credits this useful observability above weak, but no tracked automated test suite, CI, lockfile or lint/type-check setup was found. Requirements are open-ended minima; the referenced lock is absent and direct tiktoken use is undeclared. Sample evaluator truncates comparison to min row count, warns instead of failing and returns 0 despite mismatches; no response-quality or failure-path verification is demonstrated. Runtime installability and hidden-test performance remain unverified.

review.rating_anchor_scale: 0 absent; 1 weak; 2 adequate; 3 strong; 4 exceptional. Half-points indicate mixed adjacent-anchor evidence; score is anchor * 25.
review.confidence: Medium-high on source structure/static findings, medium on anchor ratings, low on untested runtime compatibility/retrieval/performance. Read all 2750 Python lines plus requirements and code README; confirmed exact clean pinned checkout. No candidate imports, installs, execution/tests, provider calls, external communications, source edits or leaderboard-score consultation.

evidence_verification: Exact quotes/line ranges and source hashes checked against the supplied full bundle at freeze time; no server-upload identity or authenticity attestation.
